body:
Retested against the latest published release on 25 October 2026: [M-Press v1.0.19](https://github.com/leaanthony/mpress/releases/tag/v1.0.19), published 5 October. Downloaded a fresh official Linux AMD64 archive, verified its SHA-256 against release checksums, and confirmed `mpress version` reports 1.0.19. Wails was rebuilt from local `releases/v3.0.0` at `18a9809b3` with `mpress build --strict --no-purge-css` (passed).

The same gaps reproduce in fresh isolated Chromium:

- 390×844: clicking the apparent “On this page” control exposes no other sections. Only Overview is visible; six section links remain `display:none`.
- 900×1000: the same inactive article section chooser.
- 390×844 with site navigation open: Home spans y=80..112 and the article bar spans y=58..100. Hit testing at the Home link centre returns the TOC instead of Home.
- 1440×1000: desktop TOC shows all seven links as expected.
- Search `CLI`: two identical CLI Reference titles/descriptions remain. Search `call Go from JavaScript`: Method Bindings remains seventh.

The documentation already pins the latest published version, so upgrading the binary alone cannot resolve these gaps. No generator or Wails source edits, new release, push, or publication were made during this retest. The local Wails and isolated M-Press task worktrees remain clean.

Implemented and tested locally in M-Press on branch `codex/mobile-toc-fix`, implementation commit `7c6308cfa6a220b2f534e37bd93f2ca6c89b56b9`. The fix is not pushed or released yet.

The generator now emits a native section disclosure with scrollable touch targets, Enter/Escape support and focus transfer to the selected heading. It positions the article bar using the actual header/sidebar geometry and hides it while site navigation is open. Existing Wails custom CSS works unchanged; new Starlight imports no longer emit the active-only section rules.

Validation:
- New browser regression fails against official v1.0.19 and passes against the candidate.
- Wails Installation and CLI pages: 390×844, 375×375, 900×1000 and 1440×1000; both themes, touch swipes to the final section, keyboard selection/focus, Escape, no-JavaScript fallback, desktop resizing and Home hit testing.
- French Installation phone/no-JavaScript checks pass.
- Wails strict builds pass with and without CSS purging: 2,031 pages; no broken links/assets. Wails source files remain unchanged.
- M-Press's own production site passes the same browser checks; public race tests, vet and current private release suite pass.
- CodeRabbit finds no production-code issues; one ledger timestamp note was addressed through the authoritative export.

The pre-existing vulnerability gate fails identically on v1.0.19 and the candidate; tracked in M-Press as `mp-b52.5.9`. This issue remains open for publication/rollout, with the responsive fix complete locally.

The tested M-Press responsive navigation fix is now pushed directly to `leaanthony/mpress` main, with no PR required:

- Implementation: https://github.com/leaanthony/mpress/commit/7c6308cfa6a220b2f534e37bd93f2ca6c89b56b9
- Main tip / validation handoff: https://github.com/leaanthony/mpress/commit/3605560c7

Focused site/importer tests passed again before pushing; remote main was a clean fast-forward from the v1.0.19 baseline. No release tag or binary release was published. Wails rollout still requires a new M-Press release and the corresponding version update.

M-Press **v1.0.20 is now published**: https://github.com/leaanthony/mpress/releases/tag/v1.0.20

The release includes the responsive article navigation fix and the patched Go 1.26.10/networking toolchain. The complete release workflow passed, including public/race/security/private checks, six archive builds, and native Linux/macOS/Windows smoke tests: https://github.com/leaanthony/mpress/actions/runs/40164725394

Downloaded the published Linux AMD64 archive, verified its SHA-256 against checksums.txt, and checked the binary version and embedded clean release revision. Rebuilt the Wails `releases/v3.0.0` checkout at `18a9809b3` with that actual published binary: 2,031 pages / 2,192 files, no broken links/assets, and the full phone/short-phone/tablet/desktop responsive navigation matrix passed in both themes, including touch, keyboard/focus, resize and no JavaScript.

Wails source files and documentation structure remain unchanged. Its existing deployment build script resolves the latest M-Press release. This verifies the fix in the generated local release site; production Wails deployment was not performed as part of the M-Press release, so this tracker remains open for that rollout and the wider UX recommendations.
